subject: 'private browser profile still held by N process(es)' at Chrome teardown under load (surface-routes.test.ts; draft-preview.browser.test.ts, syzygy-gb4l), and the /proc ENOENT seen in #228's review run

apps/three-surface-poc/src/cdp-browser.t.note: The rebase only added #228's --disable-ipc-flooding-protection launch argument; the teardown and scan code is unchanged.

diagnosis.root: [Observed] Under load, Chrome's leader acknowledges Browser.close but does not exit within the one-second grace, so teardown SIGKILLs the leader alone (12 of 30 loaded teardowns). Its helpers are then orphaned and exit on their own schedule. [Observed] At the one drain timeout, the live members were the network-service utility and two cat processes, which the /usr/bin/google-chrome wrapper forks for stdout and stderr. That matches the reported count of 3. Drains after a graceful leader exit took about 300 ms or less.
diagnosis.procScanRaces: [Observed] readdirSync('/proc', { withFileTypes: true }) lstat'ed an entry whose process had just exited, and the raw ENOENT escaped the drain. In a churn stress this happened 10 times in 2,020 scans, which matches the reviewer's ENOENT on a /proc path in #228's full run. [Observed] Once in about 5,160 scans of the variant without the Z/X skip, a dying entry read as in-group but outside our session and threw 'private browser group membership changed'. [Inferred] The kernel can report a reaped task's session as 0 while its group still reads as ours.
diagnosis.sharedRootCause: Yes for the profile-drain failures. surface-routes and draft-preview both launch through launchBrowser and both fail at closeDisposableBrowser's drain; the draft-preview failure in diagnostic run 3 had the same message as the surface-routes one.

fix: closeDisposableBrowser: once the leader has exited, SIGKILL the private process group, then each live session member a scan found, before the unchanged two-empty-scan check. killPrivateBrowserMembers signals only after a scan has seen live members, so the group id is still held and cannot have been reused.
livePrivateBrowserMembers: read plain /proc names (no lstat), and skip Z/X entries before the membership checks.

protocol.loaded: Per run, one companion full app-project vitest run (npx vitest run --project @syzygy/three-surface-poc-app --reporter=json) concurrent with the measured run of surface-routes.test.ts + polaris-generation/draft-preview.browser.test.ts. The before and final batches of 10 ran concurrently with each other, so both saw the same load (load1m 23-38 at run ends), alongside other overnight lanes. Failures are classified by message: 'STACK_TRACE_ERROR' or 'timed out in' is a timeout; 'still held' or 'profile drain' is profile-drain; an lstat /proc ENOENT or a membership/identity throw is proc-scan.
protocol.drainInstrumentation: Temporary, uncommitted logging in closeDisposableBrowser (leader killed?, live members at first scan, drain duration, outcome), run for 3 loaded runs (30 real teardowns) at the pre-fix code and again at the final code
protocol.harness: scratch scripts load.sh, frozen.mjs, churn2.mjs (not committed); raw vitest JSON retained in the session scratchpad only

results.drainNote: Pre-fix: 1 of 30 teardowns timed out (draft-preview, held by 3), and every slow drain followed a killed leader. Final: 30 of 30 drained, max 198 ms. No final teardown had helpers still alive, so these runs did not exercise the new stop path; the frozen-helper probe does.

frozenHelperProbe.method: launch, open a page, SIGSTOP this launch's network-service helper (it cannot exit on its own), then browser.close(). Committed as cdp-browser.browser.test.ts.
frozenHelperProbe.preFix: 3/3 threw "private browser profile still held by 3 process(es)" after about 4.0 s, helper left alive
frozenHelperProbe.final: 3/3 closed in about 1.1-1.2 s, 0 helpers left alive

procScanStress.method: a detached bash group forking 9 short-lived children per loop; livePrivateBrowserMembers called back to back for 6x10 s
